programme.why: One article gets read once. A programme puts your story in front of the same readers several times, each time from a new angle — that's what moves them from "seen it" to "trust it".
programme.bullet1: Keep the same core titles across waves so readers meet you again — repetition builds recall. Add one or two new titles per wave for reach.
programme.bullet2: Write a fresh article for every wave. Same story, new angle: first the problem, then the proof, then how it works.
programme.bullet3: Space waves 4–8 weeks apart — close enough to build on each other, far enough apart that each article lands on its own.
programme.anglePlaceholder: e.g. Why fleet downtime costs more than you think

angle.problem: The problem — why the status quo costs more than people think
angle.proof: The proof — a customer story or numbers that show it works
angle.howto: How it works — a practical guide readers can act on
angle.comparison: The comparison — how the options stack up, honestly

rationale.default: Three waves six weeks apart is the sweet spot for most B2B campaigns: enough repetition to build recall, enough spacing to keep each article fresh.
rationale.monthlyCycle: Your plan includes monthly titles, so waves are spaced eight weeks apart — roughly every second issue.
rationale.weeklyCycle: All your titles publish weekly, so waves can sit four weeks apart without wearing out.
rationale.launch: This reads like a launch: four tighter waves build momentum around the date.
rationale.awareness: Awareness builds slowly — waves are spaced a little wider so each article lands on its own.

programme.angleHint: The desk and writer start from this — keep it different from the other waves.

formats.title: Four ways to run native — pick the one that fits.
formats.lead: Every title in our catalog supports one or more of these four formats. The difference is whose voice you're paying for and how prominent the brand is.

native-article.title: The format you pay top dollar for.
native-article.brand: Subtle — usually a 'Sponsored by X' tag and one product mention
native-article.bestFor: Brand authority, complex sells, B2B, considered purchases
native-article.rule: If a journalist could plausibly have written this without your input, it's a native article.

advertorial.title: Your story, told inside the magazine.
advertorial.brand: Up front — brand named in dek, byline, throughout
advertorial.reads: A long-form ad with editorial styling
advertorial.bestFor: Direct response, product launches, simpler propositions
advertorial.rule: If the brand needs to be in the headline, it's an advertorial.

native-display.title: The publisher's typography, in-feed.
native-display.voice: Mostly visual — your headline, the title's layout
native-display.brand: Logo + tag in the unit; click-through to your destination
native-display.reads: An editorial card that turns out to be sponsored
native-display.bestFor: Reach and awareness against a curated audience
native-display.rule: If you want the title's frame around a click, not its words, run native display.

package.title: Article + display, one budget.
package.voice: Both — the article persuades, the display amplifies
package.brand: Subtle in the article, more visible in the display units
package.reads: A feature with its own promotion across the title
package.bestFor: Campaigns where reach inside the same title matters
package.rule: If you're already buying a native article, the package is almost always cheaper than buying display separately.

formats.disclosureTitle: All four are clearly labelled as paid
formats.disclosureBody: EU media regulators require every paid placement to be unambiguously disclosed. We default to the publisher's own disclosure label (e.g. 'Annonsørinnhold', 'Annons', 'Annonce') and verify it on every spec check before the order goes live.
formats.ctaBody: Send us a brief and the desk recommends a format mix for your goal, audience and budget — same day.

native-plus.title: Inspiration you can act on.
native-plus.voice: The title's editorial voice, with shoppable moments built in
native-plus.brand: Named advertiser; products clearly marked as buyable
native-plus.reads: A feature you can act on — tap a product, not a banner
native-plus.bestFor: Considered products where inspiration and purchase belong together
native-plus.rule: Commerce is additive, never the disguise — the story still earns the read.

content-video.title: Video that earns the play.
content-video.voice: Video in the title's register, not a TV spot
content-video.brand: Named advertiser; disclosed as paid in the player
content-video.reads: The publisher's own video, in-feed and in-player
content-video.bestFor: Stories better shown than told — demos, places, people
content-video.rule: Earns the view on its own merit; the disclosure is always visible.

productType.descNATIVE_ARTICLE: Editorial-grade article paid for by a brand, written and designed in the title's voice. Readers finish it the way they finish any other story.
productType.descADVERTORIAL: Sponsored article clearly labelled as paid content. Brand presence is up front; the surrounding design stays editorial.
productType.descNATIVE_DISPLAY: Display unit that inherits the publisher's typography and runs in-feed, not in banner slots. The trust transfer is most of the value.
productType.descPACKAGE: Bundled native article plus native display amplification in the same title — the article does the persuasion, the display does the reach.
productType.descCONTEXTUAL: Placement targeted by page topic and surrounding editorial context rather than user data — the relevance comes from where the ad runs.
productType.descOTHER: Custom or one-off format that doesn't fit the standard categories — typically negotiated case by case.
productType.descNATIVE_PLUS: Shoppable native article — editorial-grade copy with in-article product links and buy buttons, so readers can act without leaving the page.
productType.descCONTENT_VIDEO: Video-led sponsored placement that runs in the publisher's player and feed, built for attention rather than a banner slot.

advertisers.title: Buy native content across every title we cover
advertisers.lead: Discovery, comparable pricing and content production in one place. Most premium editorial inventory isn't sold programmatically — we make it bookable anyway.
advertisers.problem1Body: Thousands of titles across 9 markets, each with its own sales rep, rate card and spec sheet.
advertisers.problem2Body: Pricing lives in PDFs and emails. Comparing value across titles takes weeks of back-and-forth.
advertisers.problem3Body: Good native is editorial-grade writing tuned per publisher. Producing it in-house at quality is hard.
advertisers.solution1Body: Every newspaper and magazine that offers native, with indicative pricing, format specs and reach data — no sales call required.
advertisers.solution2Body: Submit a request to buy and our team turns it into a firm quote with the publisher. You see the price, you accept, we book.
advertisers.solution3Body: Bundled article-grade content, tuned to each title's spec and the market's disclosure rules. One supplier, better outcome.
advertisers.contentBody: Content is half the cost and most of the performance of a native campaign. Bundling it means we can ship spec-compliant, disclosure-correct articles in the lead time the publisher actually quotes — and the total bundle beats DIY.
advertisers.formatsLead: Every title in the catalog publishes some mix of these. The desk picks the one that fits the brief — and the disclosure rules of that market.
advertisers.targetingTitle: Reach the right readers by where, what, and who.
advertisers.targetingLead: Targeting on NativeSpin means choosing the right titles — not chasing people around the web.
advertisers.targetingContextBody: Pick titles by category, vertical, and editorial topic, so your story runs where it belongs.
advertisers.targetingGeoBody: Filter by market, region, city, and reach tier — national brand build or a single city.
advertisers.targetingAudienceBody: Each title carries a defined editorial audience — from regional consumers to B2B decision-makers.
advertisers.targetingHonestyBody: No behavioural retargeting, no interest graphs, no user-level data. The relevance comes from the title, not from tracking the reader.

agencies.title: A managed desk your team can lean on
agencies.lead: Plan across every title in one workspace, switch between clients in a click, and let our desk handle publisher negotiations.
agencies.feature1Body: One agency account holds every client org. Switch with one click; requests, quotes and orders stay scoped to the active client.
agencies.feature2Body: Side-by-side specs, indicative pricing and reach — built for planners, not buyers stuck in spreadsheets.
agencies.feature3Body: Where titles publish firm pricing, your planners can book instantly. Everything else routes through the desk with full transparency.
agencies.feature4Body: Surface NativeSpin inside your own client portals. Same catalog, your brand. Talk to us if you'd like early access.
agencies.workflowTitle: Same workflow your team already runs
agencies.workflowBody: Brief → plan → request → firm quote → order → live placement → reporting. We slot into the steps that hurt most — sourcing, quoting, content — without changing how you brief or report.
agencies.ctaBody: Open an agency workspace and add your clients. We'll set you up for a pilot RFQ within a working day.

publishersMkt.title: Incremental demand without building self-serve
publishersMkt.lead: We bring buyers who already understand native, hand you ready-to-publish content that meets your specs, and consolidate billing through one relationship.
publishersMkt.benefit1Body: Briefs that already know your format and lead time. No tire-kickers, no media-kit attachments.
publishersMkt.benefit2Body: Articles produced to your spec — word count, image counts, disclosure label, file formats. Spec-checked before it reaches you.
publishersMkt.benefit3Body: You own pricing and inventory. We never resell at a discount to your published rates; our margin is on the buyer side.
publishersMkt.benefit4Body: One invoice per cycle from NativeSpin across all advertisers and agencies, with payment terms you set.
publishersMkt.step1Body: We import your media kit and translate it into the NativeSpin catalog format. You verify; it goes live.
publishersMkt.step2Body: Advertisers and agencies find your titles, build a plan, and submit a request.
publishersMkt.step3Body: Our desk produces a firm quote; our content team writes the article to your spec. You see both before it's booked.
publishersMkt.step4Body: We hand over the asset and confirm placement. You publish, mark it confirmed, and we track it through to invoicing.
publishersMkt.controlBody: Block months you can't deliver in. Toggle products between firm-priced self-serve and managed RFQ. Update specs and lead times when your editorial team changes them. All from your publisher portal.
publishersMkt.ctaBody: We're onboarding titles across 9 markets. Tell us about your inventory and we'll get back within a working day.

how.title: From brief to live placement
how.lead: Five steps from "I have a campaign idea" to a published, spec-compliant native article — most of them done by us.
how.step1Body: Filter every title by market, format, category and audience. See indicative pricing and reach up front.
how.step2Body: Add titles to a plan with budget, dates and audience notes. Compare side-by-side before you commit.
how.step3Body: Submit the plan as a request. Our desk checks availability with the publisher and produces a firm quote, usually inside a working day.
how.step4Body: Our editorial team writes the article to each title's spec — length, images, disclosure label, format — and runs a spec check before it leaves the building.
how.step5Body: The publisher books and publishes. You get the live URL, tracking and an invoice with the right VAT for your market.
how.modeFirmBody: Products with firm public pricing can be booked instantly from your plan. No desk hand-off, no quote wait.
how.modeRfqBody: Indicative-priced products go through the desk. We negotiate availability and season, then give you a firm price to accept.
how.contentBody: Per-title playbooks cover tone, length, imagery, disclosure rules (Annonsørinnhold / Annons / Annonce), and brand-safety review. An automatic spec check has to pass before an asset can be marked final — so what reaches the publisher is always publishable.

about.title: Native is operationally painful. We fix that.
about.lead: NativeSpin is a marketplace for buying native content and native advertising across newspapers and magazines — including the many that don't sell programmatically.
about.missionBody1: Make native inventory as easy to find, compare and buy as programmatic display — without losing the editorial quality that makes native work in the first place.
about.missionBody2: We're buyer-first: transparent catalog, transparent pricing, managed buying behind it, content production tuned to each title. Defensibility is in the dataset and the relationships, not in any single feature.
about.whyNowBody: Native pays better than display, but the buying experience is two decades behind. Most premium titles still don't sell programmatically. Buyers and publishers both want a neutral aggregator — we're building it one title at a time in NO, SE, DK, FI, DE, AT, CH, UK and IE.
about.originBody1: Some of us have been selling native since 2006 — first for a magazine aimed at graduating students, with banners, sponsored articles and full- and half-page spreads, and later for Norway Exports, an export magazine made up entirely of native articles. Native wasn't really a category yet, and advertisers were often surprised it was even an option.
about.originBody2: Twenty years on, the picture has flipped: having native is now the norm for a title, not the exception — and the format is having its best run yet. NativeSpin is the tool we wish we'd had back then — one place to find native, compare it and buy it.
about.belief1Body: The catalog dataset and publisher relationships are the moat. Everything else is shaped around making it more complete, more accurate, more comparable.
about.belief2Body: Bad native hurts the publisher, the brand and the reader. Spec checks aren't optional and disclosure rules are encoded per market.
about.belief3Body: A managed desk only makes sense if every campaign reduces desk-hours for the next one. We instrument it so it does.
about.teamBody: A small product/engineering team in Europe, working alongside a buying desk and an editorial team for content production. We work in public — pricing, formats, disclosure rules and the partner network are all on the site.
about.contactBody: Whether you want to plan a campaign, partner as a publisher, or just compare notes on native — we'd love to hear from you.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: How NativeSpin collects, uses and protects personal data — in plain language.

controller.title: Who is the data controller
controller.body: Getia AS is the data controller for personal data processed via this marketplace. We are based in Norway and process all data inside the EU/EEA.

data.title: What data we collect
data.body: Account data (name, work email, role, organisation), marketplace activity (requests, orders, plans), and minimal telemetry needed to operate the service (login events, error reports). We do not run third-party advertising or behavioural tracking pixels on our marketing pages.

purpose.title: How we use it
purpose.body: To operate the marketplace, route requests between advertisers and publishers, produce invoices, prevent fraud, and improve the product. We do not sell personal data.

legal.title: Legal basis
legal.body: Performance of contract (account holders), legitimate interest (security, fraud prevention, product improvement), and consent (optional newsletter).

retention.title: How long we keep data
retention.body: Account data for as long as the account exists; transactional data for seven years (accounting law); telemetry rolled up to aggregates after 90 days.

sharing.title: Who we share data with
sharing.body: Publishers see the buyer organisation and order details for orders placed with them. Subprocessors (hosting, email, payments) are listed in our DPA, all EU-based or with adequate safeguards.

transfers.title: International transfers
transfers.body: Customer data is hosted in the EU. Any incidental transfer outside the EU/EEA uses Standard Contractual Clauses and an adequacy assessment.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can request access, correction, deletion or export of your personal data, and you can object to processing based on legitimate interest. Contact privacy@nativespin.com to exercise these rights.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: We use strictly necessary cookies (session, CSRF) and, with consent, anonymised product analytics. No advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.

changes.title: Changes to this policy

scope.title: Scope
scope.body: NativeSpin is a marketplace connecting advertisers and agencies with newspaper and magazine publishers offering native content and native advertising. These terms apply to all users of the marketplace.

accounts.body: You must provide accurate registration information, keep credentials confidential, and notify us of any unauthorised access. Accounts are tied to a single organisation; sharing across organisations requires the agency workspace.

liability.title: Liability
liability.body: NativeSpin facilitates the transaction but is not the publisher of placed articles. Each party is responsible for compliance with applicable advertising, disclosure and consumer-protection law. Liability is limited to the fees paid in the prior 12 months.

termination.title: Termination
termination.body: Either party may terminate the account with 30 days' notice. We may suspend or terminate accounts that breach these terms, abuse the marketplace, or fail to pay invoices.

law.title: Governing law
law.body: These terms are governed by Norwegian law. Disputes are submitted to the courts of Oslo, unless mandatory consumer-protection rules in your jurisdiction require otherwise.

changes.title: Changes to these terms

hero.pain: Most premium native isn't sold programmatically. It's sold by a phone call, a PDF rate-card, and a four-week back-and-forth. We replace that with one brief and a 24-hour firm quote.
hero.ctaMeta: No call required. We reply in writing, on the record.
hero.sideBody: Sponsored articles consistently out-perform display on attention and brand lift. Pay for what you publish, not for what's blocked.

why.h2: Native does the job display can't.
why.lead: Display buys impressions in the gutter. Native buys editorial time inside the article itself. Different real-estate, different reader behaviour, different result.
why.colABody: A sponsored article lives where the reader is already paying attention. No banner blindness, no skip button — the unit is the content.
why.colBBody: When a reader sees your story under a title they trust, some of that trust transfers. Disclosure stays clear — credibility comes from the editorial frame.
why.colCBody: A published article keeps earning impressions and search referrals after the campaign ends. Display disappears the moment you stop paying.
why.colCPull: Lives on the publisher's domain. Indexed. Permanent.

vs.primaryJobNative: Tell a story the reader chose to read
vs.primaryJobDisplay: Interrupt and redirect to your site
vs.trustTransferDisplay: None — readers know it's an ad

rule.h2: If it isn't useful to the reader, it isn't native — it's a press release in disguise.
rule.body: Every article we ship has to earn the reader's time on its own. Editorial standards, the publisher's spec, the market's disclosure label — non-negotiable. That's how the trust transfer actually works.

how.h2: Three steps. Most of the work is on our side.
how.s1Body: Target market, budget, audience, a sentence about the goal. That's enough for the desk to scope. No deck required.
how.s2Body: We come back with a title shortlist, firm pricing per publisher, content production scope, and a go-live date. Written, not on a call.
how.s3Body: We write the article to the title's spec, run the spec-check, hand you the draft for approval, then the publisher publishes. You get the live URL and an invoice.

obj.h2: What people ask before they brief us.
obj.q1: Why not just buy display? It's cheaper.
obj.a1: Per impression, yes. Per attention-second, native wins by a wide margin. If you're building consideration, the unit price isn't what matters.
obj.q2: Native feels slow. We need this in market next week.
obj.a2: Most titles publish within 10–25 days of brief. Some same-week. The 24-hour firm quote tells you exactly when, per title, before you commit.
obj.q3: We don't have the operational capacity for native.
obj.a3: That's the entire point of the desk. Brief in, finished article and live placement out. Our team handles publisher negotiation, content production, spec-checking, and invoicing.
obj.a4: We track click-throughs on every link inside your article — counted first-party. Reach (impressions) is reported by the publisher where available. We don't claim viewability or panel-based brand-lift we can't measure.
obj.q5: What about brand safety and disclosure?
obj.a5: Disclosure is encoded per market (Annonsørinnhold / Annons / Annonce) and applied automatically. Spec-check has to pass before anything reaches the publisher.

endCta.body: One paragraph is enough. We come back in writing, with a firm quote, within 24 hours.
endCta.qualPrefix: Or you're a publisher and want to be listed —

apiDocs.title: NativeSpin public catalog API
apiDocs.lead: A read API over the NativeSpin title catalog — designed for agency planning tools (Atlas-style) and adtech partners that need normalised supply data for editorial native across our 9 markets — Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, the UK and Ireland.
apiDocs.authBody: Every request carries a Bearer API key in the Authorization header. Keys are issued per integration partner by the NativeSpin team and scoped to catalog:read.
apiDocs.authRequest: Send a structured request to partners@nativespin.com — tell us the integration shape and the markets you care about, and we will issue you a key.
apiDocs.listBody: Paginated catalog listing of every active title with at least one active product. Filter by market (NO/SE/DK/FI/DE/AT/CH/UK/IE) and format (NATIVE_ARTICLE/ADVERTORIAL/NATIVE_DISPLAY/PACKAGE).
apiDocs.detailBody: Per-title detail: publisher, market (with VAT + disclosure rules), and every active product with its spec and price-rule tiers.
apiDocs.detailIncludes: Includes spec word-count bounds, disclosure label template, lead time and indicative base price in market currency.
apiDocs.paginationBody: Cursor-based on title id. Stable sort by name + id so you can run a full sync without missing rows when new titles are activated mid-sync.
apiDocs.limitsBody: Per-key bursts are smoothed through the same bucket the RFQ flow uses. A 429 response includes an approximate retry-after in the message body. Sustained high-throughput integration partners get higher limits — ask when you ask for a key.
apiDocs.errorsBody: Errors come back as JSON with a stable code and a human message. Codes today: MISSING, INVALID, EXPIRED, REVOKED, SCOPE, RATE_LIMITED, NOT_FOUND.
apiDocs.ctaBody: We will not auto-provision the API — partner integrations carry commercial implications we want to talk through first. Reach out and we will get you a working key within a working day.
apiDocs.selfServeTitle: Buy like programmatic — on named premium titles
apiDocs.selfServeBody: Discover inventory through the catalog API, then book firm-priced placements in one call — by API or in the app. No auction, no mystery supply: every title is named, every price is the publisher's. RFQ titles stay desk-mediated by design — the API places firm, self-serve inventory only.
apiDocs.ordersBody: Place a firm-priced, self-serve order. Send firm products and get a confirmed order back in one call. Requires the orders:write scope and a key bound to your organization; RFQ-only products return 422 RFQ_ONLY.
apiDocs.ordersRequest:
curl -X POST https://nativespin.com/api/v1/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"items":[{"productId":"PRODUCT_ID","quantity":1}]}'
